claims.text: The as-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has quasi-static yield strength of about 786 MPa, compressive strength of about 1314 MPa, and fracture strain of about 13.5%.
Adding about 1 at.% carbon during vacuum induction melting and homogenization will form stable nanoscale carbide precipitates in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The carbide precipitates will act as barriers to dislocation motion.
The carbide precipitates will impede crack propagation.
Carbide particles will inhibit dislocation annihilation and stabilize dislocation-cell structures.
Carbide precipitation will increase dislocation storage and strain-hardening capacity.
Carbide particles will dissipate heat and reduce the local temperature rise during adiabatic deformation.
The carbon-induced carbide microstructure will retard adiabatic shear-band localization and postpone catastrophic shear-driven failure.
The proposed improvements apply to ambient-temperature adiabatic dynamic compression at strain rates of 10^3–10^4 s^-1.
Carbon doping will raise yield strength by 10–20% relative to the baseline alloy.
Carbon doping will raise compressive strength by about 10–15% relative to the baseline alloy.
The carbon-doped alloy will have uniform ductility exceeding 13.5% strain.
Carbon doping will reduce the impact-induced energy release rate and slow rapid failure.
Approximately 1 at.% carbon is the optimal addition for the proposed strength–ductility improvement.
Carbon additions above about 1 at.% may produce excessive carbide and compromise ductility.
Carbon additions below about 1 at.% may provide insufficient precipitation strengthening and shear-band mitigation.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis claims applicability through 10^4 s^-1, but the stated conditions and falsification experiment only test 10^3–3×10^3 s^-1, leaving the upper portion of the claimed range untested.

The predicted dynamic improvements are phrased relative to quasi-static baseline values, whereas the matched experiment also uses a dynamically tested undoped control. It is therefore ambiguous whether the quantitative percentages are relative to the quasi-static values or to the undoped alloy at the same dynamic strain rate.
